text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Ministry of Supply to sell 80,000 tonnes of yellow corn worth 10 million dinars ($14.1 million) to private sector traders.
- Minister of Water and Irrigation Munzir Haddadin says poorer people would not be affected by any increases in water prices.
- Agreement in principle for merger of Bank of Jordan and Jordan Kuwait Bank, Bank of Jordan chairman Tawfiq Fakhouri says.
- Norwegian Foreign Minister Bjoern Tore Godal arrives in Amman today for talks with King Hussein.
- U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross asks King Hussein to mobilise peace talks.
- Cabinet changes water charges. Hotels, flats, hospitals, traders to pay one dinar ($1.41) per cubic metre. Rates in dry areas halved to six dinars per tanker.
- Jordan's ambassador to Iran says Tehran has not yet replied to Jordanian request for its prisoners to be freed, but says relations will improve this year.
- Ministry of Supply expected to allow private sector to import foreign cigarettes to Jordan for the first time in 20 years.
- Discussions in Paris next week expected on rescheduling Jordanian debt worth $1.2 billion.
- Soldier martyred in confrontation with infiltrators.
- King, U.S. envoy discuss efforts to reactivate stalled peace talks.
- Senate hears cabinet report on water, peace.
- King, Prince discuss defence issues with U.S. commander.
